title: Microsoft Teams: app centric management of app access in the Teams admin center for DoD
summary: The briefing's rollout facts match the roadmap record, and Microsoft Learn supports its migration warning, access controls and licensing framing. Both admin routes and the per-app PowerShell call are documented; the narrower gap about mapping org-wide toggles to PowerShell setting names was independently confirmed.

claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: App centric management in Teams Admin Center to manage the Apps access for tenants, end-users, and groups in DoD

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: App centric management defines access individually on each app using its assigned users and groups.
claims.quote: Each app contains its access definition using a list of users and groups that you assign to it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Everyone option makes the app available to existing organization users, new users and guests.
claims.quote: `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Specific users or groups restricts use to selected users and groups.
claims.quote: `Specific users or groups` | Only the users and groups that you select can use the app.

claims.claim: Guests cannot use an app set to Specific users or groups even if assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.claim: The No one availability option makes an app unavailable to every user.
claims.quote: `No one` | Not available to any user | Same as a blocked app.

claims.claim: All third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCCH and DoD deployments of Teams.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: The previous org-wide third-party app setting controlled third-party availability at organization level.
claims.quote: Org-wide app setting for third-party apps: It applies at an org-level and controls if all third-party apps are available for every user or not.

claims.claim: The previous app allow/block status controlled availability at app level.
claims.quote: App status: It applies at an app-level as allow or block and controls if it's available to any user or not.

claims.claim: The previous permission policy controlled app access at user level.
claims.quote: Permission policy: It applies at a user-level and controls if a specific user is allowed to use an app or not.

claims.claim: After switching to app centric management, the organization cannot access, edit or use permission policies.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.claim: The migration cannot be reverted.
claims.quote: Once your organization migrates, you can't revert the migration.

claims.where: Why it matters; front matter: defaultState; changes
claims.claim: Learn documents automatic tenant migration, supporting defaultState on for the arriving management change.
claims.quote: Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management.

claims.claim: Existing organizations' old settings are mapped to new access settings.
claims.quote: For existing organizations, old settings are mapped to new access settings.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Auto-migration makes an app allowed globally but blocked by a custom policy available to all tenant users in the non-EDU case.
claims.quote: except where an app is allowed in the global policy but blocked in the custom app permission policy. Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant, except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: For EDU customers the documented global/custom policy conflict instead makes the app available to none.
claims.quote: except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: Auto-migration creates one security group per custom app permission policy.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.claim: Users assigned to a permission policy are added to its corresponding migration security group.
claims.quote: All users currently assigned to an app permission policy are then added to the corresponding security group for that policy.

claims.claim: Migration assigns the groups to apps allowed by their corresponding policy.
claims.quote: These groups are assigned to each app they're allowed in their respective policy, maintaining their app access.

claims.claim: Administrators can change the resulting app assignments by managing those groups and their membership.
claims.quote: Administrators manage these groups like any others to customize the app centric management assignments, such as adding and removing users or removing the group and replacing it with another group.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings apply to new apps made available in the Teams app store.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings apply to: All the new apps made available in Teams app store.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings apply to existing apps whose availability has not been actively managed.
claims.quote: All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide settings do not override individually saved Specific users and groups assignments.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide settings do not override apps individually saved as Everyone or No one.
claims.quote: All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not apply to blocked apps.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: ... Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: Learn documents access management rather than new autonomous behavior for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" "autonomous"; read learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management and manage-apps. The described changes concern app access, assignment and migration; no new autonomous behavior is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Teams admin center does not support bulk updates of app availability.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: PowerShell with Update-M365TeamsApp can be used to update availability for many apps.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell. For more information on PowerShell cmdlets for app availability, see Update-M365TeamsApp.

claims.claim: An add action can add up to 99 users or groups at a time.
claims.quote: You can add up to 99 users or groups at a time to an app.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each organization user needs a Teams license to use Teams, except for joining meetings anonymously.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the product-level Teams license requirement.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

Read Learn app-centric-management, user-access, manage-apps and purchase-third-party-apps; no feature-specific charge found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A DoD-specific licensing statement for app centric management is not published in the checked documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" "licens" "DoD"; app centric management Teams DoD licensing price meter. Read Learn app-centric-management and user-access. The latter names TEAMS_DOD for Teams generally, not a separate entitlement for this management feature.

claims.claim: Some third-party Teams apps require their own paid service subscriptions, separate from app access management.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.

claims.claim: Learn says app centric management is not yet available to all organizations.
claims.quote: All organizations don't have the app centric management feature available.

claims.where: Scope: Clouds and rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page refers readers to MC688930 and roadmap item 151829 for timelines.
claims.quote: For timelines, see Message Center post MC688930 or Microsoft 365 roadmap item 151829.

claims.claim: Supported assignment group types include security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups and distribution lists.
claims.quote: The supported group types are security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups, and the distribution lists.

claims.claim: Learn states that using the Teams admin center requires the Teams Administrator role.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role.

claims.claim: Some administrators with higher-privilege roles can also perform app and agent governance tasks.
claims.quote: Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Previously granted admin consent to app permissions is retained after migration.
claims.quote: After migration, any admin consent to app permissions that was previously granted is retained.

claims.claim: App permissions differ from the permission policies replaced by app centric management.
claims.quote: App permissions are a different concept from permission policies, which app centric management is replacing.

claims.claim: Per-app availability is reached through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone to set app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType also accepts UsersAndGroups and Noone.
claims.quote: -AppAssignmentType: App availability type. Parameter sets: (Everyone UsersandGroups Noone)

claims.claim: OperationType Add or Remove together with Users and Groups changes user and group app assignments.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings are reached in Teams admin center through Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings.
claims.quote: To change this default setting, access Manage apps page, select Actions > Org-wide app settings, and modify the required settings.

claims.claim: Org-wide settings provide separate controls for Microsoft, third-party and custom apps.
claims.quote: Under Microsoft apps, a single control automatically enables users to install and use any available agents and apps by default. ... Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability ... Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default

claims.claim: Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings lists DefaultApp, GlobalApp and PrivateApp, but the checked Learn references do not map those names to the org-wide toggles, so no setting-specific call is given.

Read its full reference and Learn app-centric-management/manage-apps; values listed, toggle mapping absent.
